questions.text:
An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of 
focal length 15 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the 
image formed by this mirror.

criteria.description: Writes the object distance u = -10 cm and focal length f = -15 cm with correct signs
Applies the mirror formula correctly and sets up the equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with substituted values
Calculates the image position as v = +30 cm and states position of image is 30 cm from the mirror
criteria.expected_answer: v = +30 cm; position of image is 30 cm from the mirror

transcription.text:
1/v - 1/10 = -1/15
1/v = -1/15 + 1/10
1/v = (-10 + 15) / (10 x 15)
1/v = 5 / 2
v = +30 cm
Position of image formed by mirror = +30 cm on the other side of mirror.

questions.label: 24(b)
questions.text:
(b) (i) The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in 
animals. Give reasons.
(ii) State the role of phloem in the transport of materials in 
plants.

criteria.description: Gives a reason that plants have low energy needs because many tissues have a large proportion of dead cells or because plants do not move
States that phloem transports soluble products of photosynthesis (translocation) and amino acids to storage organs and growing parts

transcription.text:
The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in animals because plants are mainly composed of dead cells. Plants are stationary and don't require energy to perform activities when compared to humans animals. Moreover, simple processes like diffusion and osmosis help in transport of materials from soil. They have vascular tissues like xylem and phloem, humans animals have specialised cells
Phloem is a vascular tissue mainly composed of living cells. It helps in translocation of food. This means to transport of soluble products of photosynthesis, amino acids and hormones in plants. The flow is bidirectional. Materials like sucrose is transported by using energy from ATP for eg. During spring, food stored in stem

questions.text:
A student performs the following experiment in his school laboratory.
List two observations to justify that in this experiment a chemical change 
has taken place.

criteria.description: States the evolution of gas as an observation indicating a chemical change
States a change or rise in temperature as an observation indicating a chemical change

transcription.text:
For a chemical change to occur there has to be-
i) evolution of gas
ii) change in temperature
iii) change in odour
iv) formation of precipitate
Here,
Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2↑
Here 2 observations are seen-
i) Evolution of gas (H2)
ii) Change in temperature/since this is an exothermic reaction.

reproductive system :
(I) Ovary 
(II) Fallopian tube 
(III) Uterus 
(ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human 
males.

criteria.description: States that the ovary produces the female gamete (egg) and female hormones (oestrogen)

Names mechanical barrier (condoms) as a male contraceptive method
Names surgical method (vasectomy) as a male contraceptive method

transcription.text:
(I) Ovary →
Produces female gametes ,eggs which take part in the the process of fertilisation.

(II) Fallopian tube →
It is the site of fertilisation of female gamete (egg) and male gamete (sperm).

(III) Uterus →
Provides nutrients for nourishment of foetus. It has thick and spongy lining which provides necessary conditions if egg is fertilised. During pregnancy Placenta develops which helps to provide nutrients from mother's body and removal of waste from body of foetus.
Two contraceptive methods used by males ->
(a) Mechanical barriers - condoms
-> These help to prevent sperm transfer to female body and prevent transmission of STD's (Sexually transmitted diseases)

questions.label: 39(a)-(b)
questions.text:
The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when 
they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in 
a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These 
maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and 
break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual 
organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
(a) Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food. 1
(b) Write chemical equation involved in the above process.

spec.subject: science

criteria.notes: Full 1 mark for a correct definition; partial credit possible if definition is incomplete or partially correct, but rubric gives full mark only.
criteria.description: Names photosynthesis and defines it as the process by which green plants capture sunlight and convert it to chemical energy with the help of chlorophyll or as the process by which carbon dioxide and water are converted into carbohydrates in the presence of sunlight, chlorophyll, and water

criteria.notes: Marks for the points in order: ½, ½, 1. Check if equation is correct and balanced.
criteria.description: Writes the correct chemical equation for photosynthesis

parser_warnings: The rubric's marks (½, ½, 1) add up to 2, but points per criteria were grouped as 1 and 1 to fit the question parts. Please verify point distribution reflects teacher's intent.

a) Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants prepare their own food.
Photosynthesis is the the process by which some green plants and bacteria prepare their own food by using inorganic substances like carbondioxide and water in presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to form glucose.
6CO2 + 12H2O \xrightarrow[sunlight]{chlorophyll} C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O
glucose
